newsitem.title: TURKEY: Uighur exiles appeal to Turkish PM over riots.
newsitem.headline: Uighur exiles appeal to Turkish PM over riots.

text.p: Uighur exiles in Istanbul on Tuesday appealed to Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to intervene after at least 10 people were killed in a separatist Moslem riot last week over troubles in a region of China.
The Anatolian news agency three groups had sent a message asking for Erbakan's help on behalf of the Moslem, Turkic-speaking Uighurs in a town in northwestern Xinjiang.
Erbakan, who came to power in June in a coalition with conservatives, is modern secular Turkey's first Islamist leader.

At least 10 people were killed, including one policeman, and some 100 wounded when 1,000 Moslem separatists of the Uighur ethnic minority rampaged through Yining on Wednesday to protest against Beijing rule, Chinese sources and residents have said.
The riot was among the most violent for many years in the restive region of Xinjiang, where Turkic-speaking Uighurs are in the majority and ethnic Han Chinese make up 38 percent of the population.
